findings.title: Every context layer comes out unlocked after GordiumStart: _context_visible sets the parent Gordium::Context's IsVisible, which in Rhino 8 gives sublayers the parent's (unlocked) lock
findings.status: confirmed (reproduced in Rhino by the Rhino job; a local patch re-locking passed 13/13 claims)

skeptics: Not sent to text sceptics: confirmed by an in-Rhino run and probes (stronger than code reading). Code path verified in-session: draw_context calls _lock_context(doc, True) then _context_visible(doc, ...), which set IsVisible on every _context_layer_indexes layer including Gordium::Context itself.

findings.title: Claim 5 (reopen) never forces or asserts the layer-index shift
findings.status: refuted (one sceptic refuted: the sample lot is held on the holding layer at Look up and the layer deleted at Draw, so the shift does happen); hardened anyway in 955d97f by asserting index_after < index_before
skeptics: VERDICT: refuted. gordium_check on an empty model calls gordium_start, which draws the sample lot with _add_lot directly (not via BoxSession), saved as replaceable_lot; Look up -> apply_lookup -> lookup_may_replace -> session.hold(old) moves it to HOLDING_LAYER (creating it); Draw -> commit deletes it and remove_layer_if_empty deletes the layer; only then draw_context creates the Context layers. So the shift is set up; the only fair point is index_before != index_after is logged but not asserted.

VERDICT: confirmed. In an empty file apply_lookup holds None, so no holding layer is made and no layer is deleted; the claim never asserts index_after < index_before, so it would not distinguish the raw LayerIndex code.
